defaultUsageReason.text: Reading message history is the most common and impactful agent use case, and it triggers the most specific gates (sensitive scope review) that a developer must be aware of for production readiness.

verdict.oneLiner: Slack is a major provider with robust OAuth/OIDC support; while basic access is easy, commercial distribution with sensitive scopes (like history) requires a scope verification review, and unlisted apps face strict rate limits that act as a blocking limit for production volume.

preApprovalLimits.text: Non-Marketplace (unlisted) commercially distributed apps are limited to 1 request per minute for conversations.history and conversations.replies (max 15 objects), which blocks typical production volume.

steps.title: Gather required info and assets
steps.detail: Collect your app name, description, logo, privacy policy URL, terms of service, and list of required scopes (conversations:history, channels:read). Ensure you have a verified email and 2FA enabled on your Slack account.

steps.title: Create a new Slack app in the App Management portal
steps.detail: Log into https://api.slack.com/apps, click “Create New App”, choose “From scratch”, enter the app name and select your workspace. Accept the terms of service and complete any required identity verification (2FA).

steps.title: Configure OAuth & Permissions
steps.detail: In the app settings, go to “OAuth & Permissions”. Add the redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (claim k3). Set the required user token scopes: conversations:history, channels:read. Save changes.

steps.title: Set App Manifest (optional)
steps.detail: If using a manifest, ensure the "redirect_urls" field includes the Composio callback and that "oauth_config" lists the required scopes. This helps avoid bad_redirect_uri errors (f4).

steps.title: Link Slack app to Composio managed auth
steps.detail: In Composio, navigate to the Slack toolkit settings and select “Use my own Slack app”. Paste the Client ID and Client Secret from the Slack app’s “Basic Information” page. Ensure the redirect URL matches the one registered (k3).

steps.title: Test the OAuth flow in a sandbox workspace
steps.detail: Use a test Slack workspace to run the OAuth flow via Composio. Verify that after authorisation the token includes the requested scopes and that Composio can call conversations.history successfully. Check for rate‑limit warnings (f9).

steps.title: Submit app for Slack Marketplace review
steps.detail: In the Slack App Management page, go to “App Distribution”, fill out the marketplace listing fields (description, screenshots, privacy policy, etc.). Provide justification for requested scopes (setup_agent_drafts). Submit for review. Minimum 5 installations required (f10).

blockers.workaround: Invite the app to 5 test workspaces or ask colleagues to install.

steps.title: Await Slack review
steps.detail: During review, continue using Composio’s managed auth for existing users and test new users in a separate sandbox. Monitor for any feedback from Slack reviewers.

steps.title: Enable production mode and go live
steps.detail: Once approved, switch the Slack app status to “Live” in the Marketplace, remove any test workspace restrictions, and inform users they can now authorize via Composio at scale. Monitor rate limits; unlisted commercial apps are limited to 1 req/min (f9).

whileYouWait.text: Continue using Composio’s managed Slack auth for existing users and run integration tests in a sandbox workspace.
Prepare the marketplace listing assets (logo, screenshots, privacy policy) and draft justification for each scope.

gotchas.text: If the redirect URI does not exactly match the registered one, Slack will return a bad_redirect_uri error (f4).
Requesting sensitive scopes (e.g., calls:write) triggers an enhanced review and may delay approval (f13,f14).
Unlisted commercial apps face strict rate limits (1 req/min) which can affect production usage (f9,f12).
Switching from managed auth to your own OAuth app doesn't migrate existing connections: users reconnect, or you import their credentials where supported.

claims.text: Register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as the redirect URI (it stays on /api/v3/ even though the REST API is v3.1).

sources.quote: Register `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` as the provider's authorized redirect URI.

claims.text: Switching to your own auth config doesn't move existing connected accounts; users reconnect, or you import their credentials where supported.

sources.quote: Existing connected accounts are tied to the auth config they were created with.

claims.text: Slack has pushed the classic app deprecation deadline to November 16 2026.

sources.quote: We want to update you about our previous announcement regarding support for classic apps. After much consideration and feedback, we have decided to push back the deprecation date to **November 16, 2026**.

claims.text: Non‑Marketplace apps will have their rate limits for conversations.history and conversations.replies reduced to 1 request per minute with a maximum of 15 objects per request starting May 29 2025.

sources.quote: This rate limit reduction will apply only to applications that are commercially distributed outside of the Marketplace (also called “unlisted” apps). It will immediately impact new unlisted applications and new installations of existing non‑Marketplace applications. The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.

verifier.note: claim includes start date May 29 2025, which is not specified in the quote.

claims.text: Slack OAuth may reject scopes if the app registration does not list them as valid user token scopes, causing a pre‑install screen rejection.

sources.quote: This suggests the Slack App registration backing this client_id (...) doesn't have these scopes configured as valid user token scopes on Slack's side, so Slack drops/rejects them before the install screen.

claims.text: Using an unapproved redirect URI results in a "bad_redirect_uri" error during Slack OAuth authorization.

sources.quote: `bad_redirect_uri`: The redirect URL doesn’t match the one pre‑registered in your App Settings.

claims.text: Slack uses the OAuth authorization code flow where the user is sent to /oauth/v2/authorize and then exchanges a code for a token via oauth.v2.access.

sources.quote: Authorize: You direct the user to the corresponding /oauth/v2/authorize path... Access: Your server retrieves the verification code... and sends it to the oauth.v2.access API endpoint to exchange that code for an access token.

claims.text: Slack supports PKCE for public clients, allowing token exchange without a client secret.

sources.quote: We are excited to announce support for Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)... implement the full PKCE flow... and exchange the code using the oauth.v2.access API method without a client secret.
